newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes close up on choppy U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes close up on choppy U.S. markets.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 100 basis points at 28.50 percent on Wednesday after zigzagging through the session on pressure from hikes in U.S. long-bond yields and a weak peso, traders said.

"We were hit mainly by shaky U.S. markets, although we were expecting rates to be under pressure anyway from demand for liquidity prior to the public holiday," said a trader, referring to Thursday, when Mexican financial markets will be closed for the Virgin of Guadalupe national holiday.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds gained to 6.62 percent, compared to 6.49 percent on Tuesday.
Mexico's benchmark 48-hour peso meanwhile closed 4.3 centavos weaker at 7.9070/7.9110 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper gained in tandem with government paper to end up 50 basis points at 29.75 percent.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortfalls by injecting 7.815 billion pesos through four credit auctions, which it assigned at rates of between 29.46 and 29.78 percent.
Total credit maturities for Friday were estimated at 5.487 billion pesos.
